formula_checks.name: theBonds
formula_checks.why: Two faults and one gap. (1) AVG YIELD (bondSummary) divides interest summed over ALL bonds by value summed over all bonds. A bond with no price today still adds its full coupon to the top but nothing to the bottom, so the yield is overstated — the opposite of figure MK-NW-M-044's own rule that an unpriced bond is left out. (2) Owner rule DEC-0280 says accrued interest is subtracted when known. The formula never mentions accrued interest, so a dirty price entered as value understates every yield on today's value (M-027, M-044, M-057). (3) Gap: 'matured = years left is zero or less' and 'next maturity = earliest date that has not passed' disagree on a bond maturing today — the first calls it matured, the second can still list it as next to mature. Observation outside this card: bondRateSensitivity rounds the range to the nearest $1,000, so any bond under roughly $20,000 shows the same figure for rates up and down (a $10,000 par bond reads $10,000–$10,000 both ways) — worth a look in its own batch.
formula_checks.should_be: Average yield = Σ(face × coupon rate) over bonds WITH a value today ÷ Σ(value today − accrued interest where known) over the same bonds; bonds without a price are excluded from both top and bottom and named on screen. Yield on today's value for one bond = face × rate ÷ (value − accrued interest when known), with the 'accrued interest not entered' note when it is not. A bond maturing on today's date is matured, and 'next maturity' is the earliest date strictly after today.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0280 (2026-08-26); figure MK-NW-M-044's refusal rule; current-yield convention (annual coupon ÷ clean price); ordinary arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: theAccount
formula_checks.why: The arithmetic is right (balance as market value, income from this account's records only, untickered income at account level, transfer-in shown at the amount moved). Two cases change the answer and the formula is silent on them: (1) with no records, 'dividends + interest to the cent' sums to $0.00, but M-019 and the author's own note require no figure ('it says so instead of showing zero'); (2) ticker matching ignores capitals but says nothing about stray spaces, so a broker record 'VTI ' would match no holding and its income would vanish from the holding row.
formula_checks.should_be: Income = Σ dividends + interest in this account's records, or NO FIGURE (with the 'no records' sentence) when the account has no income records at all. Income of one holding = records whose ticker, trimmed of spaces and with capitals ignored, equals the holding's ticker trimmed the same way; a blank ticker belongs to no holding.
formula_checks.rests_on: Figure MK-NW-M-019 refusal rule; author note on M-019; ordinary string comparison.

formula_checks.name: theNetWorth
formula_checks.why: (1) Cash comes from cashTotal, which takes the uninvested cash OUT of a linked investment account; Investments comes from investmentsTotal, which counts that same account WHOLE. The uninvested cash is counted twice. The approved drawing (state A) shows Investments $354,314 = $348,495 + $5,819, i.e. WITHOUT Vanguard's $838 cash; the formula gives $355,152, and Cash + Investments + Personal property then comes to $813,990 against What you own $813,152. Two formulas describing the same money differently (cashTotal MK-NW-F-016 vs investmentsTotal MK-NW-F-021). (2) 'Return on cash + investments' is a change in balance, not a return: a deposit made inside the period is reported as if it were earned. (3) Incomplete: the type carries both monthlyDebtMinimum and monthlyDebtPayments (actual, above minimum), but the formula defines only the sum of required payments.
formula_checks.should_be: Investments = the investment slices only — for a linked account, its breakdown less its cash slice; for any other account, the whole balance when its class is an investment class — so that Cash + Investments + real assets = What you own, and Investments = Σ byClass over Stocks/Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives, Unclassified. Return on cash + investments = the time-weighted return: split the period at every deposit or withdrawal, take each sub-period's growth factor (value just before the next flow ÷ value just after the previous one, the first starting from the value on the start day), multiply the factors together and subtract 1. Refuse when a flow is recorded but the value just before it is not, since the sub-period cannot then be measured. Monthly debt payments = Σ max(stated minimum, payment set), kept separate from Σ minimums.
formula_checks.rests_on: Approved drawing 'Net worth, Quiet Instrument v08, state A'; owner DEC-0343 (a total and the sum of its parts are pinned by an invariant); owner instruction 2026-10-04: all returns are time-weighted returns (TWR); GIPS time-weighted method; author-recorded founder ruling G19.

formula_checks.name: theEmergencyFund
formula_checks.why: The mortgage is left out of debt minimums whenever the budget carries ANY rent or housing amount. That is a rule applied to money it should not touch: a household that rents its own home (budget Rent / Mortgage = its rent) and also owes a mortgage on a second property has a real, unstoppable mortgage payment dropped from both runways, and the housing-disagreement figure then compares their rent to a different property's mortgage and reports a false 'disagreement'. Also silent on: what 'enough' logged expenses means (author cites G21: average over months logged), the afterAShock arithmetic (cash after, months after, and whether a shock exactly equal to cash is covered), and whether logged expenses that already contain debt payments are de-duplicated against debt minimums.
formula_checks.should_be: Leave a mortgage's minimum out only when that mortgage IS the housing cost the budget line carries (the person's own home); any other mortgage counts in debt minimums. Report a housing disagreement only between the budget line and the mortgage on the home it describes. afterAShock: cashAfter = cash − shock; coversIt = cash ≥ shock; monthsAfter = cashAfter ÷ essentials, no figure when essentials is zero.
formula_checks.rests_on: Author note on MK-NW-M-047 ('a mortgage is never counted twice' — the purpose is avoiding double counting, which only applies to the same mortgage); founder note 2026-09-28 on M-047 ('you cannot skip a car payment'); ordinary arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: theAlternativesOutlook
formula_checks.why: As the card itself admits, the totals (isAlternative: kind list, no maturity, not property) and the rows (assetClassOf = Alternatives) use two different tests. Any account where they disagree — a person's own class answer of Alternatives on a fund whose kind is 'stocks', or a 'crypto'-kind account the person reclassified as Stocks / Funds — makes the rows not add to the total, which breaks the type's own promise ('the rows add to totalValue by construction') and author rule on M-052. The total must also equal the Alternatives slice on the Net worth tab (M-049), which is built from assetClassOf, so the totals must use assetClassOf too. Second fault: with nothing held, alternativesSummary gives a blended rate of 0, but M-051 requires no figure.
formula_checks.should_be: One test for both: the set is the accounts whose class (assetClassOf) is Alternatives. Count, total, blended rate and rows are all over that one set; total = Σ rows. Blended rate = Σ(value × benchmark for its kind) ÷ total, and NO FIGURE (not 0) when the set is empty or the total is zero; growth likewise no figure.
formula_checks.rests_on: Type comment on AlternativesOutlook.rows; author rule on MK-NW-M-052; founder 2026-09-27 'ok' recorded on M-049/M-050; refusal rule of MK-NW-M-051.

formula_checks.name: theHolding
formula_checks.why: (1) For an option, value is multiplied by 100 but total paid is not: total paid = contracts × cost per share. Option premiums are quoted per share (one contract = 100 shares), so cost basis is understated 100-fold and gain and return on cost explode (4 contracts bought at $7.35 show $29.40 paid instead of $2,940). (2) The formula never says how the long-term / short-term split is made. The US rule is 'held MORE than one year' (counting from the day after purchase); a lot held exactly one year to the day is short-term. The labels say 'over 1 yr' / 'under 1 yr', leaving exactly one year undefined. (3) Silent on sales: 'shares of every purchase added up' is only right if sold shares are removed from the lots first, and the method (first in, first out or specific lots) is not stated. (4) Day change is described per share ('last close − the close before') while M-060 describes what the holding moved in money — RULE UNCLEAR.
formula_checks.should_be: For a holding with a contract multiplier m (100 for options unless stated): value = quantity × price × m and total paid = Σ quantity × cost per share × m, so gain and return compare like with like. Long-term = lots held more than one year (sold or valued on a date later than the purchase date's anniversary); otherwise short-term. Shares and total paid are over the lots still held after sales are matched (method named). Say whether day change is per share or × shares held.
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard option contract multiplier (100 shares per equity option contract, OCC); IRS Publication 550 (2025), holding period 'more than 1 year'; ordinary arithmetic.
